# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 23 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 23 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_023_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 4, Chapter 2

**1** After I had passed the beast and gone forward about thirty feet, a young woman met me. She was adorned as if emerging from a bridal chamber — dressed entirely in white, with white sandals, a veil covering her forehead, and a turban on her head; her hair was white. **2** From my earlier visions I recognized her as the Church, and I was filled with joy. She greeted me: "Greetings, man of God!" I returned her greeting: "Greetings, my lady!" **3** She asked me, "Did nothing confront you on the way?" "Yes, my lady — an enormous beast capable of destroying peoples. But through the power and mercy of God I escaped it." **4** "You escaped well," she replied, "because you cast your anxiety upon God and opened your heart to the Lord, trusting that you could be saved through nothing other than through his great and glorious name. Therefore the Lord sent his angel — the one who has authority over the beasts, named Segri — and he shut the beast's mouth so that it could not harm you. You have escaped a great tribulation through your faith and your refusal to waver before such a terrifying creature. **5** Therefore go and tell the Lord's chosen ones about his great deeds, and tell them that this beast is a foreshadowing of the great tribulation to come. If you therefore prepare yourselves and repent with your whole hearts before the Lord, you will be able to escape it — if your hearts are pure and blameless and you serve the Lord without fault for the rest of your days. Throw your burdens upon the Lord and he will manage them. **6** Believe in the Lord, you who are double-minded — believe that he can do all things and that he turns his wrath away from you and sends plagues upon those who doubt. Woe to those who hear these words and disobey! It would have been better for them never to have been born."

---

*LOGOS note: "Woe to those who hear and disobey — better for them not to have been born" echoes Mark 14:21 (Judas) and is a rare note of solemn judgment in the otherwise mercy-focused Shepherd.*
